questions.question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 18 minutes, while pipe B can empty the completely filled tank in 20 minutes. Initially, pipe A is opened and after 6 minutes pipe B is also opened. In how much time (in minutes) will the remaining tank be filled completely?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total capacity of the tank = LCM(18, 20) = 180 units.

Efficiency of Pipe A = +10 units/min and Efficiency of Pipe B = −9 units/min.

Tank filled by Pipe A in the first 6 minutes = 6 × 10 = 60 units.

Remaining capacity to fill = 180 − 60 = 120 units.

Time to fill remaining part = 120 ÷ (10 − 9) = 120 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 120 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Time taken by Pipe A to fill the tank = 18 minutes

⇒ Time taken by Pipe B to empty the tank = 20 minutes

⇒ Time for which only Pipe A was operated initially = 6 minutes

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Total Work = LCM of individual time taken

⇒ Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

⇒ Time Required = Remaining Work ÷ Net Combined Efficiency

 
 

 **Pipe**
 **Time**
 **Total Capacity**
 **Efficiency**

**Calculations:**

⇒ In the first 6 minutes, work done by Pipe A = 6 × 10 = 60 units.

⇒ Remaining capacity to be filled = 180 − 60 = 120 units.

⇒ After 6 minutes, both pipes A and B are open together.

⇒ Net efficiency of both pipes combined = 10 + (−9) = +1 unit/min.

⇒ Time required to fill the remaining capacity = 120 units ÷ 1 unit/min = 120 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 120 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Net Efficiency

When a filling pipe (time x) and an emptying pipe (time y) run together, the net part filled per hour is (1/x − 1/y), provided the filling rate is higher than the emptying rate.

Concept of Leakage

A leakage at the bottom of a tank acts exactly like an emptying pipe. It continuously reduces the effective efficiency of the filling pipes, thereby increasing the total time required to completely fill the tank.

Alternating Pipes Method

When filling and emptying pipes are opened in alternate turns, compute the net work done in a full cycle (e.g., 2 hours). Special care must be taken towards the end, as the tank might become completely filled before the next emptying cycle begins.

questions.question: Varun and Ashish together can paint a hall in 3 days. Varun alone can paint it in 7 days. In how many days can Ashish alone paint 4 such halls?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let total work for 1 hall be LCM(3, 7) = 21 units.

Combined efficiency of Varun and Ashish = 21 ÷ 3 = 7 units/day.

Varun's efficiency = 21 ÷ 7 = 3 units/day.

Ashish's efficiency = 7 − 3 = 4 units/day.

Time required for Ashish to paint 4 halls = (4 × 21) ÷ 4 = 21 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 21 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Varun and Ashish together to paint 1 hall = 3 days

Time taken by Varun alone to paint 1 hall = 7 days

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of individual days

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time taken

Total Time = Total Work ÷ Efficiency

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 Varun + Ashish

 21 ÷ 3 = 7
 
 

 Varun
 7
 21 ÷ 7 = 3
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of Ashish = Efficiency of (Varun + Ashish) − Efficiency of Varun

⇒ Efficiency of Ashish = 7 − 3 = 4 units/day

⇒ Total work to paint 4 such halls = 4 × 21 = 84 units

⇒ Time taken by Ashish alone to paint 4 halls = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of Ashish

⇒ Time taken by Ashish = 84 ÷ 4 = 21 days

**∴ The correct answer is 21 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns

Works exactly like Time & Work. Inlet pipes have positive efficiency, while outlet pipes (leaks) have negative efficiency.

Work and Wages

Wages are strictly distributed in the ratio of the total work done by each person. If they work for the same number of days, wages are distributed in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Alternate Days Work

When people work on alternate days, calculate the total work done in one complete cycle (e.g., 2 days for 2 people) and divide the total work by the cycle work to find the number of cycles required.

questions.question: One pipe can fill the tank in 10 minutes while another pipe can empty completely filled tank in 20 minutes. If both the pipes are operated together on empty tank, how long (in minutes) will it take to fill the tank completely?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Pipe A fill time = 10 min, Pipe B empty time = 20 min

Calculations:

Total work = LCM(10,20) = 20 units

Efficiency = work/time

⇒ A = 20/10 = 2 units/min

⇒ Efficiency of B = 20/20 = 1 unit/min (empty ⇒ –1)

⇒ Net = 2 – 1 = 1 unit/min

⇒ Time = 20/1 = 20 min

**∴ Time to fill tank = 20 minutes.**

questions.question: Two pipes, A and B, can fill a tank of 7800 litres in 12 hours and 10 hours, respectively. If they are opened together, how many hours will they take to fill an empty tank of 8800 litres?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Pipe A can fill 7800 litres in 12 hours

Pipe B can fill 7800 litres in 10 hours

Total tank capacity to be filled = 8800 litres

**Formula used:**

Efficiency = Volume ÷ Time

Time taken together = Total volume ÷ (Efficiency of A + Efficiency of B)

**Calculations:**

⇒ A’s efficiency = 7800 ÷ 12 = 650 litres/hour

⇒ B’s efficiency = 7800 ÷ 10 = 780 litres/hour

⇒ Total efficiency = 650 + 780 = 1430 litres/hour

⇒ Time to fill 8800 litres = 8800 ÷ 1430

⇒ Time = (8800)/(1430) = (880)/(143) = (80)/(13)

**∴ Required time = (80)/(13) hours.**

questions.question: Robin and Varun together can paint a hall in 6 days. Robin alone can paint it in 42 days. In how many days can Varun alone paint it?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Robin and Varun together can paint in 6 days

Robin alone can paint in 42 days

**Formula used:**

Work = LCM of days taken

Efficiency = Work ÷ Time

Time taken by Varun = Total work ÷ Varun’s efficiency

**Calculations:**

⇒ LCM of 6 and 42 = 42

⇒ Total work = 42 units

⇒ Robin’s 1 day work = 42 ÷ 42 = 1 unit

⇒ Together 1 day work = 42 ÷ 6 = 7 units

⇒ Varun’s 1 day work = 7 - 1 = 6 units

⇒ Time = 42 ÷ 6 = 7 days

**∴ Varun alone can paint the hall in 7 days.**

questions.question: One pipe can fill the tank in 21 minutes while another pipe can empty completely filled tank in 24 minutes. If both the pipes are operated together on empty tank, how long (in minutes) will it take to fill one-fourth of the tank?
questions.solution:

Filling pipe time = 21 min

Emptying pipe time = 24 min

Target = 1/4 of tank

Calculation:

LCM method: Assume tank capacity = LCM of 21 and 24 = 168 units

Filling rate = 168 ÷ 21 = 8 units/min

Emptying rate = 168 ÷ 24 = 7 units/min

Net rate = 8 − 7 = 1 unit/min

⇒ 1/4 of 168 = 168 ÷ 4 = 42 units

⇒ Time = 42 ÷ 1 = 42 min

**∴ Time to fill 1/4 tank = 42 minutes**

questions.question: One pipe can fill the tank in 9 minutes while another pipe can empty completely filled tank in 90 minutes. If both the pipes are operated together on empty tank, how long (in minutes) will it take to fill half of the tank?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time taken by filling pipe to fill the tank = 9 minutes

Time taken by emptying pipe to empty the tank = 90 minutes

**Formula used:**

Total Capacity (units) = LCM of individual times

Efficiency (units/minute) = Total Capacity / Time taken

Net Efficiency = Efficiency of filling pipe - Efficiency of emptying pipe

Time = Work / Rate = Total Capacity / Net Efficiency

**Calculations:**

LCM of 9 and 90 = 90 units (Let's assume the tank capacity is 90 units)

Efficiency of filling pipe = (90)/(9) = 10 units/minute

Efficiency of emptying pipe = (90)/(90) = 1 unit/minute

Net efficiency (when both pipes are open) = Efficiency of filling pipe - Efficiency of emptying pipe

⇒ Net efficiency = 10 - 1

⇒ Net efficiency = 9 units/minute

Work to be done = Half of the tank capacity

⇒ Work to be done = (90)/(2) = 45 units

Time taken to fill half of the tank = Work to be done / Net efficiency

⇒ Time taken = (45)/(9)

⇒ Time taken = 5 minutes

**∴ It will take 5 minutes to fill half of the tank.**

questions.question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 18 minutes, while pipe B can empty the completely filled tank in 27 minutes. Initially, pipe A is opened and after 6 minutes pipe B is also opened. In how much time (in minutes) will the remaining tank be filled completely?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time taken by Pipe A to fill the tank = 18 minutes

Time taken by Pipe B to empty the tank = 27 minutes

Pipe A is opened for 6 minutes initially.

Then Pipe B is also opened.

**Calculations:**

LCM of 18 and 27 = 54 units (Let the total capacity of the tank be 54 units)

Efficiency of Pipe A (filling) = (54)/(18) = 3 units/minute

Efficiency of Pipe B (emptying) = (54)/(27) = 2 units/minute

Work done by Pipe A in the first 6 minutes = 6 minutes × 3 units/minute

⇒ Work done = 18 units

Remaining capacity to be filled = Total capacity - Work done by Pipe A

⇒ Remaining capacity = 54 - 18

⇒ Remaining capacity = 36 units

When Pipe B is also opened, the net efficiency = Efficiency of A - Efficiency of B

⇒ Net efficiency = 3 - 2

⇒ Net efficiency = 1 unit/minute

Time taken to fill the remaining tank = Remaining capacity / Net efficiency

⇒ Time taken = (36)/(1)

⇒ Time taken = 36 minutes

**∴ The remaining tank will be filled completely in 36 minutes.**

Filling pipe time = 9 min

Emptying pipe time = 90 min

**Formula used:**

Net work per minute = Inlet − Outlet

**Calculation:**

LCM of 9 and 90 = 90 units (Total capacity of tank)

Filling pipe fills 90 ÷ 9 = 10 units/min

Emptying pipe empties 90 ÷ 90 = 1 unit/min

Net work = 10 − 1 = 9 units/min

Time to fill 90 units = 90 ÷ 9 = 10 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 10 minutes.**

questions.question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 9 minutes, while pipe B can empty the completely filled tank in 10 minutes. Initially, pipe A is opened and after 3 minutes pipe B is also opened. In how much time (in minutes) will the remaining tank be filled completely?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Pipe A fills tank in = 9 min

Pipe B empties tank in = 10 min

Pipe A is opened first, and B is opened after 3 min

**Calculation:**

Assume total capacity of tank = LCM of 9 and 10 = 90 units

Work rate of A = 90 ÷ 9 = 10 units/min (filling)

Work rate of B = 90 ÷ 10 = 9 units/min (emptying)

First 3 minutes__:__ Only A works → Work done = 3 × 10 = 30 units

Remaining = 90 − 30 = 60 units

Now A and B both work together:

Net work per minute = 10 − 9 = 1 unit/min

Time to fill remaining 60 units = 60 ÷ 1 = 60 minutes

Total time to fill the remaining tank = 60 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 60 minutes.**

questions.question: One pipe can fill the tank in 7 minutes while another pipe can empty the completely filled tank in 56 minutes. If both the pipes are operated together on empty tank, how long (in minutes) will it take to fill three-fourth of the tank?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Pipe 1 can fill the tank in 7 minutes.

Pipe 2 can empty the completely filled tank in 56 minutes.

**Formula Used:**

Net work per minute = Work done by filling pipe - Work done by emptying pipe

Time to fill part of tank = (Capacity of tank × Total time) / Net work per minute

**Calculation:**

Work done by pipe 1 in 1 minute = 1/7

Work done by pipe 2 in 1 minute = -1/56

Net work per minute = (1/7 - 1/56)

⇒ Net work per minute = (8/56 - 1/56)

⇒ Net work per minute = 7/56

⇒ Net work per minute = 1/8

To fill 3/4 of the tank:

Time = (3/4 × Total capacity) / Net work per minute

⇒ Time = (3/4 × 1) / (1/8)

⇒ Time = (3/4) × 8

⇒ Time = 24/4

⇒ Time = 6 minutes

**The time required to fill three-fourth of the tank is 6 minutes.**

questions.question: A can do a piece of work in 57 hours, B and C together can do it in 28 hours, while A and C together can do it in 19 hours. How long (in hours) will B alone take to do it?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A's time to complete work = 57 hours

B and C's time to complete work = 28 hours

A and C's time to complete work = 19 hours

**Formula Used:**

Work Rate = dfrac{1}{{Time taken}}

Combined Work Rate = Sum of individual work rates

Time taken = dfrac{1}{{Work Rate}}

**Calculations:**

A's Work Rate (R_A) = dfrac{1}{57} work/hour

B and C's Combined Work Rate (R_B + R_C) = dfrac{1}{28} work/hour

A and C's Combined Work Rate (R_A + R_C) = dfrac{1}{19} work/hour

⇒ C's Work Rate (R_C) = (R_A + R_C) - R_A

⇒ R_C = dfrac{1}{19} - dfrac{1}{57}

⇒ R_C = dfrac{2}{57} work/hour

⇒ B's Work Rate (R_B) = (R_B + R_C) - R_C

⇒ R_B = dfrac{1}{28} - dfrac{2}{57}

⇒ R_B = dfrac{57}{1596} - dfrac{56}{1596}

⇒ R_B = dfrac{1}{1596} work/hour

⇒ Time for B alone = dfrac{1}{R_B} = dfrac{1}{(1)/(1596)}

⇒ Time for B alone = 1596 hours.

questions.question: One pipe can fill the tank in 18 minutes while another pipe can empty the completely filled tank in 19 minutes. If both the pipes are operated together on empty tank, how long (in minutes) will it take to fill one-third of the tank?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time taken by Pipe 1 (filling) = 18 minutes

Time taken by Pipe 2 (emptying) = 19 minutes

Find the time to fill one-third of the tank when both pipes operate together.

**Calculations:**

Let the total capacity of the tank be the LCM of 18 and 19.

LCM(18, 19) = 18 × 19 = 342 units

So, Total Capacity of the tank = 342 units.

Efficiency of Pipe 1 (filling pipe) = Total Capacity / Time taken by Pipe 1

⇒ Efficiency of Pipe 1 = 342 units / 18 minutes = 19 units/minute (filling)

⇒ Efficiency of Pipe 2 = 342 units / 19 minutes = 18 units/minute (emptying)

Net efficiency when both pipes are operated together = Efficiency of Pipe 1 - Efficiency of Pipe 2

⇒ Net efficiency = 19 units/minute - 18 units/minute = 1 unit/minute

One-third of the tank capacity = (1/3) × 342 units

⇒ Required Work = 114 units

Time taken to fill one-third of the tank = Required Work / Net efficiency

⇒ Time taken = 114 units / 1 unit/minute

⇒ Time taken = 114 minutes

∴ It will take 114 minutes to fill one-third of the tank.

questions.question: A can complete a piece of work in 18 days and B can complete it in 22 days. If they work on alternate days, starting with B on the first day, then in how many days will the work be finished?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A can complete work in = 18 days

B can complete work in = 22 days

They work on alternate days, starting with B on the first day.

**Calculations:**

Let the total work be the LCM of 18 and 22.

Prime factorization of 18 = 2 × 3 × 3 = 2¹ × 3²

Prime factorization of 22 = 2 × 11 = 2¹ × 11¹

LCM(18, 22) = 2¹ × 3² × 11¹ = 2 × 9 × 11 = 198 units

So, Total Work = 198 units.

Efficiency of A = Total Work / Time taken by A

⇒ Efficiency of A = 198 units / 18 days = 11 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of B = 198 units / 22 days = 9 units/day

They work on alternate days, starting with B.

Work done in one 2-day cycle (Day 1 by B, Day 2 by A):

Work done in 2 days = 9 + 11 = 20 units

Number of complete 2-day cycles to finish work close to 198 units:

Number of cycles = Total Work / Work per cycle

⇒ Number of cycles = 198 / 20 = 9 with a remainder of 18 units.

So, after 9 complete cycles (9 × 2 = 18 days):

Work done in 18 days = 9 × 20 = 180 units

⇒ Remaining work = 198 - 180 = 18 units

Now, on Day 19, it's B's turn (since B started and 9 cycles ended with A).

Work done by B on Day 19 = 9 units

Remaining work after Day 19 = 18 - 9 = 9 units

Total days passed = 18 + 1 = 19 days

On Day 20, it's A's turn.

A's efficiency = 11 units/day

Time taken by A to finish remaining 9 units = Remaining Work / A's efficiency

⇒ Time taken by A = 9 / 11 days

Total time to finish the work = 19 days + 9/11 days

⇒ Total time = 19(9)/(11) days

∴ The work will be finished in 19(9)/(11) days.

questions.question: Pipes A and B can fill an empty cistern in 84 minutes and 36 minutes, respectively. Both Pipe A and Pipe B are opened together. After how much time should Pipe B be turned off so that the empty cistern is completely filled in a total of 42 minutes?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time taken by Pipe A to fill the cistern = 84 minutes

Time taken by Pipe B to fill the cistern = 36 minutes

Both pipes are opened together, and the cistern should be completely filled in 42 minutes. We need to find the time after which Pipe B should be turned off.

**Formula used:**

Efficiency of a pipe = 1 / Time taken to fill the cistern

Work done by a pipe in 1 minute = Efficiency of the pipe

**Calculations:**

Efficiency of Pipe A = 1 / 84 (portion of the cistern filled by Pipe A in 1 minute)

Efficiency of Pipe B = 1 / 36 (portion of the cistern filled by Pipe B in 1 minute)

Let Pipe B be turned off after t minutes. In the first t minutes, both pipes A and B work together, and in the remaining (42 - t) minutes, only Pipe A works.

The total work done by both pipes is 1 (to completely fill the cistern), so we can write the equation:

Work done by Pipe A in 42 minutes + Work done by Pipe B in t minutes = 1

Work done by Pipe A in 42 minutes = 42 × (1 / 84) = 1/2

Work done by Pipe B in t minutes = t × (1 / 36) = t / 36

Now, set up the equation for total work done:

(1/2) + (t / 36) = 1

⇒ t / 36 = 1 - 1/2

⇒ t / 36 = 1/2

⇒ t = (1/2) × 36 = 18

**∴ Pipe B should be turned off after 18 minutes.**

questions.question: A can finish a work in 2 days and B can do the same work in 52 days. B worked alone for 26 days and left the job. In how many days can A alone finish the remaining work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A can finish a work in 2 days.

B can finish the same work in 52 days.

B worked alone for 26 days and left the job.

**Formula Used:**

Work = Rate × Time

LCM method for combined work calculation.

**Calculation:**

Work done by A in 1 day = 1/2

Work done by B in 1 day = 1/52

LCM of 2 and 52 = 52

Total work = 52 units (assuming the work as a whole unit divided into 52 equal parts).

Work done by B in 26 days = 26 × (1/52)

Work done by B in 26 days = 26/52

Work done by B in 26 days = 1/2

Remaining work = Total work - Work done by B

Remaining work = 1 - 1/2

Remaining work = 1/2

A's efficiency = 1/2 work per day.

Days required by A to finish remaining work:

⇒ Remaining work / A's efficiency

⇒ (1/2) / (1/2)

⇒ 1 day

**A alone can finish the remaining work in 1 day.**

questions.question: One pipe can fill the tank in 19 minutes while another pipe can empty the completely filled tank in 21 minutes. If both the pipes are operated together on empty tank, how long (in minutes) will it take to fill two-third of the tank?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

One pipe can fill the tank in 19 minutes.

The other pipe can empty the completely filled tank in 21 minutes.

**Calculation:**

The LCM of 19 and 21 is 399. So, the total capacity of the tank = 399 units.

Efficiency of the filling pipe (first pipe) = 399/19 = 21 units/minute

Efficiency of the emptying pipe (second pipe) = 399/21 = 19 units/minute

Since the second pipe is emptying the tank, its efficiency is negative.

Combined efficiency = Efficiency of the filling pipe - Efficiency of the emptying pipe = 21 - 19 = 2 units/minute.

Total work (to fill two-thirds of the tank) = (2/3) × 399 = 266 units.

Time taken = Total work / Combined efficiency = 266 / 2 = 133 minutes.

**∴ It will take 133 minutes to fill two-thirds of the tank.**

questions.question: Pipes A and B can fill an empty cistern in 72 minutes and 76 minutes, respectively. Both Pipe A and Pipe B are opened together. After how much time should Pipe B be turned off so that the empty cistern is completely filled in a total of 54 minutes?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Pipe A fills the cistern in = 72 minutes

Pipe B fills the cistern in = 76 minutes

Both pipes are opened together.

Total time to fill the cistern = 54 minutes

**Formula used:**

Total Capacity (Work) = LCM of individual times

Efficiency = Total Capacity / Time taken

Work done = Efficiency × Time

Remaining Work = Total Capacity - Work done

**Calculations:**

Let the total capacity of the cistern be the LCM of 72 and 76.

Prime factorization of 72 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 = 23 × 32

Prime factorization of 76 = 2 × 2 × 19 = 22 × 191

LCM(72, 76) = 23 × 32 × 191 = 8 × 9 × 19 = 72 × 19 = 1368 units

So, Total Capacity = 1368 units.

Efficiency of Pipe A = 1368 units / 72 minutes = 19 units/minute

⇒ Efficiency of Pipe B = 1368 units / 76 minutes = 18 units/minute

Pipe A works for the entire duration of 54 minutes.

Work done by Pipe A in 54 minutes = Efficiency of A × Time A worked

⇒ Work done by A = 19 units/minute × 54 minutes = 1026 units

⇒ Work done by B = 1368 - 1026 = 342 units

Time for which Pipe B worked = Work done by B / Efficiency of B

⇒ Time for which Pipe B worked = 342 units / 18 units/minute

⇒ Time for which Pipe B worked = 19 minutes

Pipe B should be turned off after this much time.

**∴ Pipe B should be turned off after 19 minutes.**

**Given:**

Pipe A = 72 min, Pipe B = 76 min, Total = 54 min

**Formula used:**

Work = rate × time

Calculation:

A alone for 54 min does = dfrac{54}{72}=dfrac{3}{4}

Remaining work = 1 - 3/4 = 1/4

Extra rate when B is also open = Rate(B) = dfrac{1}{76}

Need x min of both so that x × Rate(B) = 1/4

⇒ xtimesdfrac{1}{76}=dfrac{1}{4}

⇒ x=dfrac{1}{4}×76=dfrac{76}{4}=19

**∴ Turn off Pipe B after 19 minutes.**
